title: Verity County Health Department
description: Food inspection reports with the scores and the violation text as written, septic permits, autumn immunization clinics and free well water testing. One sanitarian, one vacancy, and a health officer who is here eight hours a week.

data.motto: Environmental health, immunization and communicable disease for the seven towns and the three townships.
notices: IMMUNIZATION CLINICS, OCTOBER AND NOVEMBER 2026. Gridfall: Tuesday 6 October and Tuesday 20 October, 9:00 AM to 12:30 PM, at this office, 41 Depot Street. Marchfield: Thursday 1 October and Thursday 15 October, 1:00 to 4:30 PM, in the meeting room at the Marchfield Public Library, 114 Ward Street. Use the Ward Street ramp door. The front steps are not the way in for the meeting room and people go up them anyway. Coyne Flats: Thursday 5 November, 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM, Grange hall. No appointment and no charge. See [url=/s/immunization]Immunization Clinics[/url] for what to bring and what we can give.

Inspection reports are published here within ten business days of the inspection. Reports for inspections conducted between 13 July and 21 August 2026 went up late, some of them by four weeks. The Department is funded for two sanitarian positions and has had one vacant since March. Publication is what is behind. Enforcement is not: where action is taken it is taken on the day of the inspection, and a suspended permit is suspended whether or not the report has appeared on this page.

Free bacteriological and nitrate testing for private wells runs from Thursday 1 October to Friday 20 November 2026. One sample per household. The allocation is 240 bottles and when the bottles are gone the offer is over, which in 2025 was 6 November. Bottles are picked up at the counter and must come back within 30 hours. Do not bring a sample on a Friday. See [url=/s/well-water]Private Well Water Testing[/url].

There is a site at [url=synth://verityfoodhandler.click/]verityfoodhandler.click[/url] selling a "Verity County Food Handler Certificate" for $69.95 with a seal on it that is not ours. It is not issued by this Department, it is not recognised by this Department, and no establishment in the county is required to accept it. Nine people have brought one to the counter since June. The Department's card is $15, is good for three years, and is printed while you wait. See [url=/s/food-handler]Food Handler Training Card[/url].

Automated answers about county services may be produced by [url=synth://ask.verity.ai/]VerityAssist[/url]. The Department does not write those answers, does not review them and is not able to correct them. Two have reached this office often enough to be worth stating here. This Department does not issue well drilling permits; those are issued by the state. The on-site wastewater permit fee is $185, not $60. The $60 figure was the fee in 2009.

Inspection reports from 2016 through March 2024 were published on the previous county portal and were not migrated to this one. Paper copies are held here and may be read at the counter without an appointment. Copies are $0.25 a page. Permit processing times for 2024 and 2025 were compiled and released on Friday 12 June 2026 under Records Request 2026-041 (H. Brenner) and the released tables are listed under [url=/s/septic-permits]On-Site Wastewater (Septic) Permits[/url].

Main number 782-4090. Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, closed 12:00 to 12:45. Option 3 on the recorded menu, marked environmental health, has gone to an extension that does not exist since the phone system was changed in February. Press 0 and ask. The Department has reported this twice and has been told both times that the menu is maintained by the vendor.

The Ashkettle and Coyne Flats clinics are reached on Route 7, which is running a detour and is not serving the Depot and Quarry stop. Check [url=synth://verity-transit.gov/s/route-7]the Transit Division's Route 7 page[/url] before you plan on it. The Marchfield clinic is a short walk from the Marchfield town hall stop on Route 4.

Public bathing place permits for the 2027 season open on Monday 1 February 2027. The 2026 season closed on Monday 7 September. Two of the county's four permitted pools did not operate in 2026 and neither has said whether they intend to in 2027.

services.name: Inspection Reports - August and September 2026
services.blurb: Every routine, follow-up and complaint inspection of a permitted food establishment in the current publishing period, with the score and the observations as written. Thirteen reports.
steps: Find the establishment by its trading name. Reports are filed under the name on the sign, not the name of the owner or the corporation, because that is the name people look for.
Read the date. A report describes what an inspector saw on one day. It is not a rating of the establishment and the Department does not publish one.

Read the score against the key. [b]90 to 100[/b] satisfactory. [b]80 to 89[/b] satisfactory with follow-up, and the follow-up is on the named violation only. [b]70 to 79[/b] conditional, reinspection within ten days. [b]Below 70[/b] unsatisfactory, reinspection within 72 hours and the permit may be suspended on the spot.

Read the violation classes. A [b]priority[/b] violation is five points and is something that can make a person ill by itself, such as a holding temperature or a bare-hand contact. A [b]priority foundation[/b] violation is three points and is something that lets a priority violation happen, such as a missing thermometer or no test strips. A [b]core[/b] violation is one point and is maintenance, cleaning or paperwork.
A low score with everything corrected on site is a different thing from a high score with a priority violation left open, and the arithmetic will not tell you which you are looking at. Read the text.

Reinspection results are written into the bottom of the original report rather than published separately. If a report mentions a reinspection, the reinspection happened and its score is in the same paragraph.
To ask about a report, or to get one that is not here, call 782-4090 and ask for environmental health. Do not use option 3.
To report a problem at an establishment, use [url=/s/complaints]Food Illness and Sanitation Complaints[/url]. A complaint is inspected, not filed.

services.name: Inspection Reports - Earlier Periods
services.blurb: Reports older than the current publishing period. Most of them are on paper in this office and can be read at the counter. There is no search.
steps: Decide which period you need. Anything from April 2024 onward is in the current system and staff can print it while you wait.
Anything from 2016 to March 2024 is in one of seven binders at the counter. Ask for the binder by town and year.

Anything before 2016 is in boxes at the county records annex and takes five to seven business days. Request it on Form VC-5 through [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/records-request]the county public records service[/url], not here, because the annex is not ours.
Copies are $0.25 a page at this counter. The county annex charges $0.15 a page for the same copy. Nobody here can explain that and it has been raised.
If you are looking for a specific inspection and you know roughly when it was, say so. The binders are chronological and the fastest way through them is a date.

services.name: Food Establishment Permits and Plan Review
services.blurb: The permit you need to sell food to the public in Verity County, what it costs, and the plan review that comes before it if you are building or remodelling.
steps: Work out your category before you pay anything. [b]Category 1[/b] is prepackaged only, $95 a year. [b]Category 2[/b] is limited preparation, no cooling of cooked food, $160. [b]Category 3[/b] is full service, $310. [b]Mobile unit[/b] is $180 and needs a commissary agreement. A caterer is Category 3 no matter how small the kitchen is.

If you are building, remodelling or changing category, submit plans for review [b]before[/b] you buy equipment. Review is $120 and takes about three weeks. Two rejections this year were over a hand sink that could not be reached from where the food was prepared, which is a wall, not a fitting.
Submit Form VCH-2 with the plan review approval, the menu, and the name of the certified food protection manager. A Category 3 permit is not issued without a certified manager named on it.
The Department inspects before opening. That inspection is included in the fee. Ask for it at least five working days out and understand that in July and August it may be more.
Permits run to 31 March and are not prorated. A permit taken out in February costs the same as one taken out in April. This has been raised with the Board twice.
Pay at the counter or through [url=synth://verity.county.gov/]the county services portal[/url]. The portal adds a 2.4 percent vendor fee. The counter does not, and takes a cheque.
A permit is issued to a person and a place. It does not transfer when the business is sold. Buyers find this out at closing more often than they should.

forms.name: Food Establishment Permit Application (Form VCH-2)
forms.note: Fillable PDF, four pages. Page 3 asks for the make and model of every refrigeration unit. Give the serial number too if you have it; it saves a phone call later.

forms.name: Plan Review Application (Form VCH-2P)
forms.note: PDF. Submit with a floor plan to scale, a finish schedule and an equipment list. Hand-drawn is accepted if it is to scale and dimensioned. Four of the last ten approved plans were hand-drawn.

forms.name: Change of Ownership Notification (Form VCH-2X)
forms.note: PDF, one page. Must be received before the change, not after. There is no fee. The new owner still applies for a new permit.

forms.name: Certified Food Protection Manager, list of accepted programmes (one page)
forms.note: Six accepted programmes. The list has not changed since 2019 and two of the six no longer run a course within 90 miles.

forms.name: Fee schedule, effective 1 April 2026 (one page)
forms.note: Adopted by the Board of Health on 10 February 2026. The previous schedule was adopted in 2017.

services.name: Food Illness and Sanitation Complaints
services.blurb: How to report suspected foodborne illness or an unsanitary condition at a permitted establishment. Complaints are inspected, not filed.
steps: Call 782-4090 and ask for environmental health, or fill out Form VCH-9 at the counter. Complaints may be anonymous and most of them are.

Tell us the establishment, the date and time you were there, and what you ate or what you saw. If several of you ate together, say what each person had, including anyone who did not get ill. That comparison is the only thing that makes a food history useful.

If you are ill, see a clinician and ask for a stool culture. Without a laboratory confirmation the Department can inspect but cannot attribute. Most complaints end here and that is not a brush-off, it is what the evidence supports.

A complaint about a temperature, a person working while ill, or a sewage problem is inspected within one business day. A complaint about cleanliness is inspected at the next routine inspection unless there is something specific in it.
We do not tell the establishment who complained. We cannot stop an establishment from working out who complained if four people ate there that day.

You will not usually be told the outcome, because the outcome is somebody else's inspection report. The report itself will appear under [url=/s/inspection-results]Inspection Reports[/url] with 'complaint' in the line.

forms.name: Food Complaint Form (Form VCH-9)
forms.note: One page, paper at the counter or by phone. There is no online version. The online version was budgeted in 2021 and the money went to the well testing allocation instead.

forms.name: Food History Worksheet (Form VCH-9H)
forms.note: Two pages, 72 hours of meals. Staff fill this out with you over the phone and it takes about twenty minutes. Nobody enjoys it.

forms.name: Complaint log, 2026 year to date (summary, one page)
forms.note: 61 complaints received. 22 inspected within one business day. 4 resulted in a violation being written. 1 resulted in a suspension. 0 laboratory-confirmed outbreaks.

services.name: On-Site Wastewater (Septic) Permits
services.blurb: New systems, repairs and replacements outside the sewer districts, plus how to get a copy of the permit and the as-built drawing for a property you are buying.
steps: For a new system: a soil evaluation first, by a registered evaluator, in the ground, at the location of the proposed field. A perc test from a neighbouring lot is not a soil evaluation for your lot and will be rejected.

Submit Form VCH-40 with the evaluation, a site plan showing the well, the property lines, any surface water within 100 feet, and the proposed field. The fee is $185. A repair permit is $90. A replacement is $185.

Review is running eleven to fourteen weeks against a published target of four. The backlog is a staffing matter and the Department will not pretend otherwise. Permits for a failing system that is discharging to the surface are moved to the front and are being issued in three to six working days.

The system is inspected before it is covered. Have the installer call for the inspection with at least two working days' notice and do not backfill. Systems backfilled before inspection are uncovered at the owner's cost and this happens five or six times a year.

[b]Getting a copy of an existing permit.[/b] Search by parcel number, not by your name. Permits before 2001 are indexed under the name on the application, which is usually the installer or the person who owned the land when the system went in, and for most houses that is not you. Bring the parcel number from your tax bill or from [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/land-records]the county land records service[/url] and staff can find it in a few minutes.

If there is genuinely nothing on the parcel, the system predates permitting, which in this county means before 1973. That is not a defect and it is not a violation. Lenders are told this in writing on request and Form VCH-40N exists for exactly that.

The as-built drawing is a separate sheet from the permit and is sometimes filed in the wrong year. If the permit is there and the as-built is not, say so and staff will check the two years either side before telling you it is missing.
There are people who will offer to expedite this for a fee, including one at [url=synth://countypermits-fast.vip/]countypermits-fast.vip[/url]. Nobody can expedite it. There is one reviewer.

forms.name: On-Site Wastewater Permit Application (Form VCH-40)
forms.note: Fillable PDF, six pages including the soil log sheet. Page 5 must be signed by the registered evaluator in ink. A typed name is not a signature and the application will come back.

forms.name: Existing System Records Search (Form VCH-40R)
forms.note: One page. Free. Give the parcel number. Results in two to five business days, or at the counter while you wait if it is after 2001.

forms.name: No Record of Permit letter (Form VCH-40N)
forms.note: Issued on request when a search finds nothing. States the date of the search, the parcel searched and the year permitting began. Most lenders accept it. Two do not and the Department cannot help with that.

forms.name: Abandonment of a Septic Tank (Form VCH-44)
forms.note: One page. Required when a property connects to a sewer district or a tank is taken out of service. The tank must be pumped and the lid collapsed or the tank filled. $40.

forms.name: Permit processing times, 2024 and 2025 (three pages, released 12 June 2026)
forms.note: Released under Records Request 2026-041 (H. Brenner). Median days from complete application to permit: 2024, 38. 2025, 61. First half of 2026, 79. The tables count complete applications only, which is why they do not match the counter's experience; an application returned for a missing signature restarts at day zero and 22 percent of them are.

forms.name: Map of the three sewer districts (one page)
forms.note: Gridfall, Marchfield and the New Carrow village district. Everything else in the county is on-site. The map was drawn in 2008 and the New Carrow boundary has been extended twice since.

services.name: Registered Installers, Pumpers and Soil Evaluators
services.blurb: The current registry. Registration means the person has met the Department's requirements. It is not a recommendation and the Department does not keep a complaint record you can read.
steps: [b]Registered installers, 2026.[/b] Bregger Excavating (Marchfield). Hollander Septic Service (Ashkettle), [url=synth://hollanderseptic.synth/]hollanderseptic.synth[/url]. Kerrin Earthworks (Kerrin). Lindenau and Sons (Gridfall). Tarbell Excavating (Coyne Flats). Vetter Construction (Halsey, registered June 2026).

[b]Registered pumpers, 2026.[/b] Hollander Septic Service. Pell Valley Sanitation (out of county, registered here). Tarbell Excavating. Dorrance Pumping (Nye Mills, registered for pumping only, not installation).

[b]Registered soil evaluators, 2026.[/b] G. Bregger. M. Tarbell. R. Ostrowski (also registered in two adjoining counties). D. Kilbride, R.S. (Department staff, evaluations for repair permits only, no charge, and the backlog on those is the same backlog).

Registration lapses on 31 December and about a third of the list renews in the last week of the year. A name missing in January is usually a renewal that has not been processed, so call before you assume.
The Department does not rank installers, does not maintain a list of ones to avoid, and will not tell you on the phone which one to use. Ask your neighbours. In this county that works.

A dispute about workmanship is a civil matter. The Department can only act if the installed system does not match the permit, and if you think it does not match the permit, say that, because that we can inspect.

forms.name: Installer Registration (Form VCH-41)
forms.note: Annual. $75. Requires proof of liability insurance and one system inspected and passed in the previous two years.

forms.name: Soil Evaluator Registration (Form VCH-42)
forms.note: Annual. $75. Requires the state evaluator credential, which the Department does not issue and cannot look up for you.

forms.name: Pumper Registration and Disposal Log (Form VCH-43)
forms.note: Annual, $75, with a monthly disposal log. Septage goes to the Marchfield treatment plant and nowhere else. The log is checked against the plant's receiving records twice a year.

services.name: Immunization Clinics
services.blurb: Walk-in clinics in Gridfall, Marchfield and Coyne Flats through October and November. Childhood schedule, adult tetanus, influenza and shingles. No appointment, no charge for the childhood schedule.
steps: [b]Gridfall.[/b] Tuesday 6 October and Tuesday 20 October, 9:00 AM to 12:30 PM, at this office, 41 Depot Street. Park in the lot off Depot; the two spaces at the door are for the nurse's car and the vaccine cooler.

[b]Marchfield.[/b] Thursday 1 October and Thursday 15 October, 1:00 to 4:30 PM, in the meeting room at the Marchfield Public Library, 114 Ward Street. In by the Ward Street ramp door. The library posts its own closures at [url=synth://marchfieldlibrary.blog/]the library's blog[/url] and if the building is shut the clinic is shut.

[b]Coyne Flats.[/b] Thursday 5 November, 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM, Grange hall, 7 Grange Road. This is the only north-end clinic this autumn. The Milbrook clinic was not scheduled because the room is not available and no alternative was offered.
Bring the child's immunization record if you have it. If you do not have it, come anyway. We can nearly always find the record in the state registry and it takes about four minutes.

Childhood schedule vaccines are free to any child in the county regardless of insurance. Adult tetanus and diphtheria is $32. Influenza is $25 and free to anyone 65 or over or on public assistance. Shingles is $205 and most private insurance pays it at a pharmacy for less, so ask there first.
We cannot give travel vaccines, rabies pre-exposure, or anything requiring a prescription from your own clinician. Yellow fever is not given anywhere in this county or the two next to it.
School exemption paperwork is signed at the clinic if the medical part is already completed by a clinician. The Department cannot complete the medical part.

[b]If you are on the bus.[/b] The Marchfield clinic is a short walk from the Marchfield town hall stop on Route 4. The Coyne Flats clinic is on Route 7, which is on detour. See [url=synth://verity-transit.gov/s/route-7]the Route 7 page[/url] for the stops that are actually being served.

forms.note: Two pages, filled in at the clinic. It can be downloaded and brought completed and that saves about ten minutes at the table.

services.name: Private Well Water Testing
services.blurb: Bacteria, nitrate and hardness testing for private wells. Free from 1 October to 20 November while the bottle allocation lasts, and $28 the rest of the year. About 4,900 households in this county are on a private well.
steps: Pick up a bottle at the counter, or ask for a kit to be mailed. The bottle contains a preservative tablet. Do not rinse it, do not touch the inside of the cap, and do not use your own jar. A sample in a jar is thrown away and that is the second most common reason a test fails.
Sample from a cold tap that has no filter, no softener and no aerator on it. The outside spigot is usually the right one. Take the aerator off if there is one; do not just run it harder.
Run the tap for five minutes first. Fill to the line, not to the top. Cap it and write the date and time on the label while you are standing there.

[b]The sample must reach the laboratory within 30 hours of being taken.[/b] The courier collects from this office Monday through Thursday at 2:00 PM. A sample handed in after 2:00 PM on Thursday sits until Monday and the bacteriological result is reported as invalid, which means you did the work for nothing. That is why the Department asks you not to bring one on a Friday.

Results are emailed within nine business days, or posted on paper if you ask. Bacteriological results are read as present or absent, not as a number. Nitrate is reported in milligrams per litre and the drinking water limit is 10.

If a result is out of range a sanitarian calls you the same day and stays on the phone until you know what to do next. This is a person and they will call back if they miss you. In 2025 that was 214 calls out of 1,142 samples.

A single positive for total coliform is usually the tap, the hose or the sampling, not the well. Resample before you shock-chlorinate anything. A positive for E. coli is different and is treated as urgent.

Testing is recommended once a year, and after any flooding, any work on the well, or any change in how the water tastes or looks. Most households in this county test once, when they buy the house, because the lender made them.

This service is also listed on [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/well-water]the county services portal[/url]. That listing is accurate except for the drop-off points: the coolers at the Halsey and Milbrook town halls were withdrawn in 2025 and are not being restocked. The Department has asked twice for the listing to be corrected.

forms.name: Well Test Kit Request (Form VC-101)
forms.note: This is a county portal form, not one of ours, and it still works. One page, about ninety seconds. Kits are mailed within three business days.

forms.name: Sample Submission Slip (Form VCH-31)
forms.note: Comes with the bottle. Fill in the time of collection, not the time you dropped it off. The laboratory uses that time to decide whether the sample is valid.

forms.name: Well Disinfection Instructions (two pages)
forms.note: Chlorine quantities by well diameter and depth, with the arithmetic done for the six common cases. Written in 1998 and reviewed in 2014. Still correct.

forms.name: Nitrate and Infants (one page)
forms.note: The short version: do not make formula with water over 10 milligrams per litre of nitrate, and do not boil it to fix it, because boiling concentrates it. The Department will test any household with a pregnancy or an infant free of charge at any time of year.

forms.name: Laboratory certification, Pell Valley Analytical (certificate copy)
forms.note: State-certified for drinking water bacteriology and nitrate. The Department has used this laboratory since 2011 and the contract is rebid every three years. Nobody else bid in 2024.

services.name: Food Safety at Home and at Public Events
services.blurb: Temperatures, cooling, home canning and church suppers. The handouts here are the ones the Department gives out at the counter and they have not changed much because the numbers have not changed.
steps: [b]Four temperatures worth knowing.[/b] Cold food at or below 41F. Hot food at or above 135F. Poultry cooked to 165F. Ground meat cooked to 155F. A whole cut of beef or pork is 145F and a rest. Everything else on this page follows from those.

[b]Cooling is what actually makes people ill.[/b] Cooked food has to get from 135F to 70F within two hours, and from 70F to 41F within four more. A stockpot of chili in a home refrigerator does not do this; it takes nine or ten hours and the middle of it sits in the range where bacteria multiply for most of them. Divide it into pans no more than two inches deep, uncovered, and cover it once it is cold. This is the single most common priority violation written in this county.

[b]Thaw in the refrigerator, under cold running water, or in the cooking process.[/b] Not on the counter. A turkey on the counter overnight is the one the Department gets asked about every November and the answer has not changed.

[b]Leftovers.[/b] Four days in the refrigerator. Reheat once, to 165F, all the way through, not just at the edge. Reheating in a slow cooker does not get there fast enough; use the stove or the oven and then hold it in the slow cooker.

[b]Home canning.[/b] Low-acid foods, which is nearly all vegetables, all meats and most soups, need a pressure canner. A boiling water bath does not reach the temperature that matters and no amount of time in one will make up for it. Tomatoes are borderline and need added acid. The Department tests dial gauges free of charge at the counter, takes about ten minutes, and in 2025 four of the 38 tested were reading more than two pounds off.

[b]Church suppers, fire department barbecues and fundraisers.[/b] If it is open to the public and food is sold or donations are taken, it needs a temporary event permit. See [url=/s/temp-events]Temporary Food Event Permits[/url]. If it is a members-only potluck it does not, and the Department still recommends two probe thermometers and a hand washing station because the bacteria do not check the guest list.

[b]Cottage food.[/b] Baked goods that are not potentially hazardous, jams, jellies and dry mixes may be made in a home kitchen and sold direct to the consumer without a permit, up to $35,000 a year, with a label that names you and gives your address. Cheesecake, cream pies, anything with meat and anything that needs refrigeration are not cottage foods and are not close.
[b]A meat thermometer costs about nine dollars.[/b] The Department has given away 400 of them in the last three years and would rather do that than write the violation.

forms.name: Cooling and Reheating (one page, both sides)
forms.note: The two-stage cooling rule with a chart and four worked examples including a 20 quart pot of chili. This is the handout the Department prints most of.

forms.name: Safe Internal Temperatures (refrigerator card)
forms.note: Card stock, magnet strip on the back. Free at the counter. About 300 a year go out and the Department is happy about that.

forms.name: Home Canning: what needs a pressure canner (two pages)
forms.note: Reviewed against the national guidance in 2014. The acidity table is the part people come back for.

forms.name: Dial Gauge Testing (walk-in service)
forms.note: Bring the lid or the gauge to the counter, any weekday morning. No charge, no appointment, ten minutes. Weighted gauges do not need testing and cannot be tested.

forms.name: Cottage Food Operations (three pages)
forms.note: What is allowed, what is not, the label requirements and the sales limit. Updated when the state updated the limit in 2023. The Department gets about one call a week on this, mostly about cheesecake, and the answer is still no.

services.name: Food Handler Training Card
services.blurb: The county food handler card. $15, valid three years, printed at the counter the same day. Required for anyone who handles unpackaged food in a permitted establishment.
steps: Sit the course. In person at this office on the first Tuesday of the month at 9:00 AM, about ninety minutes, no booking needed for fewer than four people. Or take the written packet home, work through it and bring it back.
Pass the twenty-question test. The pass mark is fifteen. It may be retaken the same day, once, free. Almost everybody passes.
Pay $15 in cash, by cheque, or by card at the counter. The card is laminated and handed to you before you leave.

The card is valid three years from the date of issue and is yours, not your employer's. It goes with you when you change jobs. Employers who keep the card when someone leaves are keeping something that is not theirs and the Department will reissue it free once in that situation.

An establishment must have at least one carded person on every shift. A Category 3 establishment must also have a certified food protection manager, which is a different, longer and more expensive qualification and is not this.

[b]The card is not sold online.[/b] There is no online version and no third party is authorised to issue it. The certificate sold at [url=synth://verityfoodhandler.click/]verityfoodhandler.click[/url] for $69.95 is not this card and is not accepted here.
Courses in Spanish are run twice a year, in March and October, and the packet is available in Spanish at any time. Ask at the counter.

forms.name: Food Handler Course Packet (28 pages)
forms.note: Print or collect at the counter. Handwashing, temperatures, cross contamination, cleaning and sanitizing, employee health. Written in 2016 and it reads like it.

forms.name: Food Handler Test (Form VCH-15)
forms.note: Twenty questions, multiple choice. Taken at the counter under staff observation. Not sent out, not taken at home, not emailed.

forms.name: Replacement Card (Form VCH-15R)
forms.note: $5, or free if your employer kept the original. Bring identification. The Department can look up a card issued since 2015.

forms.name: Course dates, October 2026 to March 2027 (one page)
forms.note: First Tuesday of the month at 9:00 AM: 3 November, 1 December, 5 January, 2 February, 2 March. The October course was moved to Tuesday 13 October because the immunization clinic has the room that morning.

services.name: Temporary Food Event Permits
services.blurb: Two-day permits for fairs, suppers, barbecues and fundraisers where food is sold or donations are taken. $35, or no charge for a volunteer fire department, a school or a church.
steps: Apply at least ten days before the event on Form VCH-7. Late applications are taken up to two days before and cost $35 extra, which is not a penalty, it is the overtime.

Say what you are cooking and where you are cooking it. A menu of hamburgers cooked to order is a different permit conversation from a menu of anything cooled overnight, and cooling overnight at an event is usually refused.

You need a hand washing station: a container with a spigot, warm water, soap, paper towels and a catch bucket. A hand sanitizer pump is not a hand washing station. This is the most common thing people turn up without.
You need a probe thermometer, and somebody who will use it. Two if you are cooking in more than one place.

Food is prepared at the event or in a permitted kitchen. It is not prepared at home. The exception is baked goods that are not potentially hazardous, which may come from a home kitchen, and that exception is where most of the confusion lives.
The Department inspects most events during service, against a nine-item checklist, and temporary events are not scored out of 100. The checklist is on the back of the permit.

Standing events keep a file. The Ashkettle Volunteer Fire Department's July barbecue has a file going back to 2005 and has never had a violation recorded against it; their own page is at [url=synth://ashkettlevfd.org/fundraiser]the department's fundraiser page[/url]. The county fair's food court is permitted as fourteen separate temporary events, which is how the state counts it, not how the fair counts it.

forms.name: Temporary Food Event Application (Form VCH-7)
forms.note: Two pages. Page 2 is the menu and the equipment list and is the part that gets the application approved or returned.

forms.name: Nine-item event checklist (one page)
forms.note: Printed on the back of the permit. Hand washing, thermometers, holding temperatures, protection from contamination, water supply, wastewater, ice handling, worker health, cleaning. Read it before the day.

forms.name: Annual Event Registration (Form VCH-7A)
forms.note: For an organisation that runs the same event every year. Covers one event a year for three years at $60 total. Eleven organisations in the county are on it.

forms.name: 2026 permitted events list (two pages)
forms.note: Ninety-one temporary events permitted between 1 April and 20 September 2026. Fourteen of them are the fair.

services.name: Animal Bites and Rabies Specimen Submission
services.blurb: What to do after a bite, how an animal is confined and observed, and how a specimen is submitted to the state laboratory. Call the same day. Do not wait for office hours if it is a wild animal.
steps: Wash the wound with soap and running water for fifteen minutes. This is not a formality and it is the single most effective thing anyone does in the whole sequence.
See a clinician. County General's emergency department handles this and so will an urgent care. The decision to begin post-exposure treatment is a clinical one and is not made by this Department.

Report the bite. 782-4090 during office hours. Outside office hours, call the sheriff's dispatch non-emergency line and ask for the health officer on call. There is one, every night, and it is not always the same person.

[b]A dog or cat that can be identified is confined and observed for ten days.[/b] If it is alive and well on day ten, there was no rabies exposure, regardless of its vaccination status. The animal is not destroyed for testing. This is the answer to the question the Department is asked most often about this.

[b]A wild animal, or a stray that cannot be confined, is a different matter.[/b] Bats, raccoons, skunks and foxes are the ones that matter here. A bat in a bedroom where someone was asleep is treated as an exposure even if nobody saw a bite.

Do not damage the head. A specimen is not testable if the skull has been crushed or if the animal has been frozen and thawed repeatedly. Refrigerate it, do not freeze it, double bag it, and call before you drive anywhere.
Specimens go to the state laboratory. The Department packages and ships them. Results are usually back in two working days and the Department calls you either way.

Dog licensing requires a current rabies certificate and is done through [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/dog-license]the county portal[/url], not here. The Department runs a low-cost rabies vaccination clinic each spring, next one Saturday 17 April 2027, $12 a dog or cat.

forms.name: Animal Bite Report (Form VCH-60)
forms.note: Completed by the Department from your phone call. Clinicians and veterinarians submit their own copy. You do not need to fill this in yourself.

forms.name: Confinement and Observation Order (Form VCH-61)
forms.note: Served on the animal's owner. Ten days, at home if the animal is licensed and vaccinated, otherwise at a veterinary practice at the owner's cost.

forms.name: Rabies Specimen Submission (state form RL-12)
forms.note: State form, not ours. The Department completes it. Kept here because people ask for it by number.

forms.name: Bat in the House (one page)
forms.note: How to contain a bat without damaging it, why it matters, and when it is an exposure. Printed in 2009. The Department gets between eight and twenty of these calls a summer.

services.name: Public Bathing Places
services.blurb: Permits and inspections for public and semi-public pools. The 2026 season closed on 7 September. Four pools are permitted in the county and two of them did not open this year.
steps: The 2027 season permit application opens Monday 1 February 2027 and must be in by 1 April. The fee is $220 a pool.

A permitted pool is inspected before opening and twice during the season, plus any complaint. Disinfectant residual, pH, clarity, the main drain cover, the fence and the gate latches, the rescue equipment and the operator's certificate.

The operator must hold a current pool operator certificate. The Department does not run that course and the nearest one is 70 miles away, which is why two of the four pools are late with it every year.

A pool closes immediately if the main drain cover is not intact, if the bottom cannot be seen from the deck, or if there is a faecal accident, and it does not reopen until the Department has been back.

The Gridfall municipal pool and the Marchfield school pool operated the full 2026 season. The New Carrow village pool and the Halsey motel pool did not open. Neither has said whether they will in 2027 and the Department has no power to make them.

forms.name: Public Bathing Place Permit (Form VCH-70)
forms.note: Annual, $220. Opens 1 February. Includes the pre-season inspection.

forms.name: Daily Operating Log (Form VCH-71)
forms.note: Kept by the operator, checked at every inspection. Two readings a day minimum, more on a hot Saturday. Logs filled in on Monday for the whole previous week are visible from across the room and are written up every time.

forms.name: 2026 season inspection summary (one page)
forms.note: Two pools, nine inspections, three closures, all three for disinfectant residual out of range, all three reopened the same day.

services.name: About the Department, Staff and the Board of Health
services.blurb: Who works here, what the Department can and cannot do, when the Board meets, and where the budget went.
steps: [b]Office.[/b] 41 Depot Street, Gridfall, in the annex behind the county building. Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, closed 12:00 to 12:45. The counter is the first door on the right and there is a bell.

[b]Staff.[/b] Health Officer, Dr. M. Ruhl, eight hours a week under contract, also health officer for two other counties, in this office on alternate Wednesdays. Director of Environmental Health, G. Voss. Registered Sanitarian, D. Kilbride, R.S. Second sanitarian position, vacant since 13 March 2026, posted three times. Public Health Nurse, B. Rademacher, R.N., four days a week. Clerk, J. Tolliver, who answers the phone and who is the reason anything gets found.

[b]What the Department does.[/b] Food establishment permits and inspections. On-site wastewater. Private well water. Public bathing places. Immunization. Communicable disease investigation. Rabies. Temporary events. Body art establishments, of which the county has two.

[b]What the Department does not do.[/b] Animal control, which is the sheriff. Air quality and open burning, which is the fire marshal through [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/burn-permit]the county portal[/url]. Public water supplies, which are the state. Well drilling permits, also the state. Nuisance complaints about long grass, junk vehicles and noise, which are code enforcement and which this office receives about forty of a year and forwards.

[b]Board of Health.[/b] Five members, appointed by the Board of Supervisors, serving three years, unpaid. Meets the second Tuesday of the month at 7:00 PM at 41 Depot Street. Agendas are posted at the counter and on the county portal five days before. Public comment is taken at the start, three minutes each, and in the last two years the number of people who have used it is nine.

[b]Budget.[/b] The Department's 2026 appropriation is $612,400, which is 1.9 percent of the county budget and is $4,100 less than 2019 before inflation. Permit and licence fees bring in about $148,000 of it. The vacant sanitarian line is funded and has been each of the three years it has been posted.

[b]Records requests.[/b] Anything not on this site goes through Form VC-5 at [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/records-request]the county records request service[/url]. This Department answers 30 to 40 a year and most of them are somebody buying a house.
